_: Every field the model config accepts, with the value to use when the feature is switched on. Not a runnable config: it lists
options that exclude each other, and the per-domain values below cannot both apply. Copy the keys you need. Keys starting with
'_' are documentation and are dropped at load.
_rir_domain: 'spectrogram' diffuses on the two-channel real/imaginary STFT, 'waveform' on the raw RIR as a 1 x T image. It sets in_channels,
out_channels and sample_size, so it fixes weight shapes and must stay recorded for inference.
_rir_gain: x_0 is multiplied by this before noising and divided by it after denoising, so the schedule sees a standard deviation near 1.
1.0 for spectrogram, whose sigma is already 0.50; 15.127 for waveform at full decay flattening. Re-measure with
debug/sigma_gain_probe.py whenever the signal or the flattening changes.
_block_out_channels: One entry per resolution level, each halving the spatial size. [32, 64, 128] for spectrogram. Waveform needs the
depth to reach a useful receptive field: [32, 32, 64, 64, 128, 128, 256, 256, 256].
_layers_per_block: ResNet layers per level; a single int, or a list with one entry per level.
_use_cross_attention: One bool per level, or null to let the model decide — which puts cross-attention on level 0 only, where the
conditioning has the most spatial detail to act on.
_attention_head_dim: Channels per attention head; a single int, or a list with one entry per level.
_norm_num_groups: GroupNorm groups, or null to let the model pick the largest divisor of every block width, preferring 32.
_use_mid_block: The middle block at the lowest resolution. false removes it.
_channels: 2 for spectrogram (real and imaginary), 1 for waveform. Both must match rir_domain.
_use_cond_encoder: An MLP over the scalar condition vector. false feeds the raw vector to the UNet.
_encoder_hidden_dims: Hidden widths of that MLP; the last entry is the embedding the UNet receives.
_src_trgt_dist_cond: Appends the speaker-to-microphone distance to the condition vector, raising input_cond_dim by 1. The distance is
implied by the positions, but stating it saves the network from deriving it.
_section_pos_encoder: Fourier Positional Encoder (applied before the condition MLP)
_pos_encoder_cfg: enable: false drops the encoder and feeds the raw scalars.
encode_mode: 'full' encodes every entry of the condition vector; it is the only mode implemented.
n_freqs / max_freq_log2 / log_scale: 6 frequencies spaced by powers of two up to 2^4, which resolves room-scale geometry.
include_raw: keeps the unencoded value alongside the encoding, so coarse magnitude survives.
input_norm: per-entry divisor bringing physical units near 1, in condition-vector order — room L/W/H, microphone x/y/z,
speaker x/y/z, RT60, distance. Metres for the geometry, seconds for RT60.
_fusion_enable: false trains on the scalar conditions alone, leaving the image encoder unused.
_image_fusion: How image tokens reach the UNet. 'cross_attn' attends to them at every level that carries attention.
_image_encoder_config: model_variant: 'large' is ViT-L at 1024 dims, 'base' is the smaller backbone.
feature_mode: 'pyramid' takes several depths, 'last_n' the final n layers, 'single' the last only. Depth matters
because geometry and material read at different layers.
last_n: how many layers 'last_n' and 'pyramid' draw from.
layer_combination: 'fuse' sums the layers into one token set, 'stack' concatenates them and multiplies the count.
spatial_pool_factor: null keeps every patch token; an integer pools the patch grid by that factor. This is the lever
to pull when VRAM is tight, rather than shrinking image_size.
image_size: must match the rendered images. [224, 294] for Matterport3D, a 16 x 21 = 336-patch grid per image.
_guidance_enabled: Trains the conditional and unconditional model together so the sampler can interpolate between them. Required for
any guidance scale above 1 at inference.
_guidance_dropout_prob: Share of training steps that drop the conditioning.
_section_loss: Loss Weighting — the noise loss alone when omitted, null, or method 'none'
_loss_weighting: {'method': 'rt60_binary', 'db_threshold': -40.0} drops the loss past rt60 * |db_threshold| / 60 seconds, so it stops
scoring the part of the window the RIR has already decayed through.
Untried. The cutoff assumes a straight decay and reads the stored rt60, and every fit window under-reads by 10-30%,
so it lands earlier than the threshold implies.
_section_c50_loss: Clarity Loss Term — off when omitted or null
_c50_loss: Adds weight * |C50(prediction) - C50(reference)| in dB, both measured on the un-scaled waveform with the estimator the
Tried at 5.93e-05 and 2.37e-04 and neither improved C50; the larger weight was the less harmful. Off in the golden.
weight: pick it from the ratio of gradient norms against the noise loss with debug/c50_weight_probe.py, never from the
two loss values, which are in unrelated units.
min_snr_gamma: caps the per-sample weight min(SNR(t), gamma). The coded SNR assumes x_0 has standard deviation 1; at
the spectrogram's 0.50 the true ratio is 4x smaller, so gamma 20 clamps where gamma 5 is meant to. Use 5 only when
eps: added to both energies before the log, bounding the gradient where either approaches zero.
_section_edc_loss: Energy Decay Curve Loss Term — off when omitted or null
_edc_loss: Adds weight * the mean squared difference between the predicted and reference decay curves. Each curve starts at its own
signal's peak and is normalised by the energy of the window the two share, so the term reads decay shape alone.
Cut EDC distance by 27% but moved C50, DRR, EDT and fitted T60 the wrong way, so the golden leaves it off.
form: 'db' reads the curves in decibels, which weights the quiet late decay; 'linear' compares them as they are, putting
most weight in the first 50 ms. 'db' was the better of the two.
weight: has no transferable value, since the two forms differ by orders of magnitude and the ratio depends on the model.
floor_db: clamps both curves this far below their start, ending each sample's comparison where its decay has run that
far and bounding the logarithm's gradient. 30 dB reaches half the rt60.
min_post_peak_ms: the shortest shared post-peak window a sample may be measured over; shorter pairs sit out of the term.
energy_floor: the window energy below which a sample carries no curve to compare, and the lower bound on the energy
